title: The Quest to Understand the Forgotten Psychedelic
gist: An introduction to mescaline, the cactus-derived compound that gave psychedelics their name and has thousands of years of documented Indigenous ritual use in the Americas, framed around one of the first brain scans of the drug (not detailed in this excerpt).

insights.claim: Psychiatrist Humphry Osmond coined the term 'psychedelic' in a 1956 letter to writer Aldous Huxley, a few years after Osmond took his first mescaline trip.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Establishes mescaline as the etymological and historical origin point for the entire term 'psychedelic.'
insights.quote: Psychiatrist Humphry Osmond coined the term in a letter to writer Aldous Huxley in 1956, a few years after he took his first mescaline trip.

insights.claim: In a follow-up letter to Huxley, Osmond wrote the now-famous rhyming couplet: 'To fathom Hell or soar angelic, just take a pinch of psychedelic.'
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: A specific documented quote capturing how the drug's discoverer-namer described its dramatic and unpredictable effects.
insights.quote: To fathom Hell or soar angelic, just take a pinch of psychedelic.

insights.claim: Mescaline, derived from cacti like peyote in North America and San Pedro in South America, generates vivid visuals, deep emotional connectedness, and a dream-like state.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Describes the core subjective effects of the compound that shaped the broader cultural definition of 'psychedelic.'
insights.quote: Known to generate vivid visuals, deep emotional connectedness, and a dream-like state, it’s played a critical part in ritual practices in Indigenous societies throughout the Americas, including the Aztec and Huichol, for millennia.
insights.locator: Some say mescaline isn't just the original psychedelic

insights.claim: Some researchers consider mescaline not just the original psychedelic in name but the first psychedelic substance ever used by humans, with archaeological evidence of peyote use tracing back more than 5,000 years.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Places mescaline's human use timeline among the longest documented for any psychoactive substance, underscoring its historical and anthropological significance.
insights.quote: Archaeological evidence of peyote use, in particular, traces back more than 5,000 years.
insights.locator: Some say mescaline isn't just the original psychedelic
